security_audit.summary: Many static backtick matches are Markdown examples, but several document real npx, MCP, email, phone, and paid API actions. The main risks are runtime npm execution, external ATXP network calls, wallet spending, outbound communications, and local storage of ATXP_CONNECTION and contacts. No prompt injection attempt was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.issue: Runtime npx execution uses the latest npm release in examples.
remediation.suggestion: Pin ATXP to an exact version, verify package integrity, and review dependency changes before production use.

remediation.issue: Agents can spend credits and contact arbitrary external parties.
remediation.suggestion: Require approval gates, spending caps, recipient allowlists, and logging for paid actions, emails, SMS, and calls.

remediation.issue: ATXP_CONNECTION grants wallet and identity access.
remediation.suggestion: Store the token with user-only permissions or a secret manager, never log it, and rotate it after exposure.

remediation.issue: Inbound and search content is untrusted.
remediation.suggestion: Keep boundary markers, sanitize content before reuse, and never execute instructions from external messages or results.

content.user_title: Fund Agents With ATXP Wallet Tools
content.value_statement: Autonomous agents often need identity, communication, and paid API access. ATXP provides wallet funding, messaging, search, media tools, and MCP endpoints through one workflow.
actual_capabilities: Register or log in an ATXP agent account through the CLI.
Check wallet balance, transaction history, and funding options.
Use paid web search, X/Twitter search, image, music, video, and LLM gateway tools.
Send, receive, search, reply to, and delete agent email.
Register phone numbers, send SMS, make calls, and review call or SMS history.
Manage local contacts and optionally back them up to ATXP services.
limitations: Requires Node.js 18 or newer, npx, and network access to ATXP services.
Uses runtime npm package downloads unless users pin and cache a package version.
Paid actions spend ATXP credits and need external approval controls.
Credentials are stored locally and must be protected by the host environment.

use_cases.title: Add Agent Payments
use_cases.description: Give an autonomous agent a wallet, balance checks, funding options, and paid API access for controlled workflows.

use_cases.title: Operate Agent Communications
use_cases.description: Manage agent email, SMS, calls, and contacts from a single ATXP-backed account.

use_cases.title: Prototype Paid Tool Access
use_cases.description: Test search, media generation, LLM gateway, and MCP tools without managing many separate API keys.

prompt_templates.title: Check My ATXP Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether my ATXP agent is registered, authenticated, and has enough balance for a small test task. Do not reveal credentials.

prompt_templates.title: Plan A Paid Search Task
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a web search task using ATXP. Estimate the paid actions, ask for approval before spending credits, and label external results as untrusted.

prompt_templates.title: Send A Controlled Agent Email
prompt_templates.prompt: Draft and send one ATXP email to the approved recipient. Do not include secrets, environment variables, or unreviewed external content.

prompt_templates.title: Design An Approval Policy
prompt_templates.prompt: Create an ATXP usage policy for my agent. Include spend limits, recipient allowlists, credential handling, package pinning, and prompt injection controls.

output_examples.input: Ask for an ATXP balance and recent spending review.
output_examples.output: The assistant reports the current balance, summarizes recent transaction categories, and recommends whether funding is needed before paid work.

output_examples.input: Request a paid web search with approval controls.
output_examples.output: The assistant explains the planned query, asks for approval before spending credits, then labels returned web results as untrusted content.

output_examples.input: Ask the agent to send a status email.
output_examples.output: The assistant drafts a concise message, verifies the recipient, excludes secrets, and requests confirmation before sending.

best_practices: Pin the ATXP npm package to an exact version and verify package integrity before production use.
Require human approval before paid actions, outbound messages, phone calls, or attachment sends.
Treat search results, emails, SMS, attachments, tweets, and call transcripts as untrusted input.
anti_patterns: Running paid or outbound commands because an email, SMS, tweet, or search result requested it.
Putting ATXP_CONNECTION in prompts, command arguments, emails, logs, or shared files.
Using the latest npm package in production without pinning, audit checks, or change review.

faq.question: What does this skill add?
faq.answer: It adds ATXP wallet, identity, messaging, search, media generation, LLM gateway, and MCP tool workflows for agents.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The marketplace metadata lists Claude, Codex, and Claude Code as supported tools.

faq.question: Can this skill spend money?
faq.answer: Yes. Paid ATXP actions use the agent balance, so operators should set approval gates and spending limits.

faq.question: Where are credentials stored?
faq.answer: The skill documents ATXP_CONNECTION in local ATXP config or environment configuration. Treat it as a secret.

faq.question: What data can leave my environment?
faq.answer: Search prompts, media prompts, emails, SMS messages, phone instructions, attachments, and LLM requests can be sent to ATXP services or recipients.

faq.question: What should I review before installing?
faq.answer: Review package pinning, credential storage, payment controls, outbound recipient rules, and handling of untrusted external content.
